subject: DPA: proposed incident alert window & forensic handover (prelim 24h / 7bd snapshot)
messages:
From: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@finservlegal.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Audrey Lim <audrey.lim@finservanalytics.com>, security@finservanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: proposed DPA wording for incident notifications and forensic access

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the time on Friday. As we prepare to finalize the Master DPA, legal asked me to surface a few practical asks on incident notification and evidence handover so our InfoSec team can satisfy their audit.

High-level asks from FinServ Analytics: 
- Preliminary alert within 24 hours of confirming an incident that may affect customer data (timing can be local business hours).
- A limited "forensic snapshot" transfer within 7 business days for triage, with a commitment that Redwood will preserve full telemetry/backups for at least 90 days.
- Clear minimal-scope definition: evidence only includes logs, telemetry buckets and process snapshots directly related to the impacted tenant. No broad export of production data.
- Subprocessor cooperation clause: any subprocessor must accept the same notification commitments and allow evidence access or a validated export path.
- Cross-border note: where transfers are restricted, we expect Redwood to provide equivalent operational evidence or an attestation from the subprocessor.

I've attached a redline (FinServ_DPA_redline_v3.docx) with inline edits. Can you confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with a 24h preliminary alert and 7 business day snapshot for limited evidence? If not, please propose alternate windows and any gating conditions.

Best,
Jane Sullivan
Counsel, FinServ Analytics

Subject: Re: Initial: proposed DPA wording for incident notifications and forensic access

Jane — thanks for the clear asks and the redline. We're aligned on the goal: give you actionable evidence quickly while limiting blast radius and protecting other customers/subprocessors.

Quick answers up front:
- 24h preliminary alert: OK in principle, provided "confirming an incident" has a narrow operational definition (we suggest "credible evidence of a security event materially affecting customer data" — happy to draft language).
- 7 business day forensic snapshot: may be tight for some subs and depending on timezones, but we can commit to a preliminary forensic snapshot within 7 business days for Redwood-managed telemetry and runbook artifacts. For third-party subprocessors we may need to map timelines by provider.
- 90-day preservation hold: acceptable as a baseline; we typically preserve 180 days for some telemetry types but can contract to 90 days for this DPA.

Can @Ben and @Kimberly weigh in on subprocessor constraints and legal redlines? Also looping Laura for commercial alignment.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Karthik — legal review below (high level). I'll prepare suggested wording to limit obligations while keeping FinServ comfortable.

Notes: 
- 24h preliminary alert: acceptable if we define "preliminary" as a notice of investigation rather than conclusive breach. i.e., language: "preliminary notice of suspected incident affecting customer data". We should reserve the right to narrow based on confidence level.
- 7 business day snapshot: acceptable for Redwood-owned artifacts and logs. For subprocessor-held data (S3 buckets / managed DBs) we must honor their contract timelines; propose adding a phrase: "to the extent reasonably available from Redwood-managed systems; for subprocessor-held data, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain or provide alternative evidentiary attestation within the same timeframe."
- Evidence minimal scope: we should explicitly list categories (system logs, service-level telemetry, relevant request traces, config snapshots) and prohibit full dataset exports.
- Jurisdiction/cross-border: recommend clause allowing production of equivalent operational evidence (aggregated/hashed indicators) where export is restricted and adding an obligation to escalate to legal within 24 hours of any refusal.

I'll draft a redline to attach back. @Ben — can you confirm if 7 business days is operationally feasible for the initial snapshot for our typical infra (GCP/us-east)? Any gotchas for partners with longer retention/backfill windows?

-kim
Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Short operational note: 7 business days is feasible for a scoped forensic snapshot for Redwood-managed telemetry and our standard request/forensics playbook. Key constraints to call out in the DPA: 
- We need a written request with tenant and incident identifiers to trigger evidence collection. Verbal alerts are fine to start triage but snapshot timelines will start upon written request.
- Subprocessors: several of our partners (managed DB vendor, certain observability providers) have contractual notice windows of 10-15 business days for production exports. We can try to accelerate but must avoid promising timelines we can't meet.
- We can commit to 90 days preservation and temporary evidence escrow for high-risk incidents subject to procurement of escrow services (cost to be negotiated).

Operational ask for FinServ: include a technical contact and a short runbook snippet in the contract (email + PagerDuty ID) to ensure the request is properly routed.

Ben Carter
Head of Incident Response, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick responses — helpful. Two clarifications from our side: 
1) Written trigger: fine; we'll accept the tenant+incident ID requirement.
2) Subprocessor timelines: FinServ is sensitive to long delays. If a subprocessor cannot meet the 7 business day snapshot, we expect: (a) a written attestation of the subprocessor's timeline, and (b) a plan for an equivalent operational attestation (hashes, indicators, or redacted metadata) within 7 business days.

We'll attach the FinServ technical contact and a short runbook snippet in the next upload. Jane will also upload the redline with a few alternate phrasing options.

—Audrey
Sr. Product Security Manager, FinServ Analytics

Subject: Re: DPA: proposed incident alert window & forensic handover (prelim 24h / 7bd snapshot) — next steps

Team — thanks for the constructive back-and-forth. Summary and proposed contract language items we will submit back to you next week: 
1) "Preliminary notice" = notice of suspected incident; Redwood will provide a preliminary alert within 24 hours of credible evidence, and a conclusive incident determination within 72 hours where possible.
2) "Forensic snapshot" = Redwood-managed logs, request traces, and config snapshots limited to the impacted tenant. Snapshot delivery: target 7 business days for Redwood-managed data upon a written request containing tenant and incident id; for subprocessor-held data Redwood will provide a written attestation of expected timeline and commercially reasonable efforts to obtain equivalent evidentiary attestation within 7 business days.
3) Preservation: Redwood will maintain a preservation hold for 90 days for data related to the incident; operationally we may retain some telemetry up to 180 days, but the contract baseline will be 90 days.
4) Minimal scope and redaction: we'll add explicit prohibitions on bulk exports of unrelated customer data and limit exports to fields necessary for investigation (we'll enumerate categories).
5) Escrow/forensic access: offer optional paid escrow for expedited exports when required by regulation (procurement to set terms).

Next steps: Kimberly will produce a concise redline addressing the subprocessor/attestation language and the written-request trigger. Ben will attach a technical appendix describing the snapshot contents and delivery mechanics. Laura will confirm commercial language on escrow costs. We aim to return a single counter-redline by Wed, Oct 28.

If that timeline works for FinServ, please confirm and we'll proceed.

-Karthik
Sr. Director, Customer Security Operations, Redwood Inference
